title: David's prophecy: Hear, O daughter

edition.locus: Vossius 1684 Opera omnia, Latin column, In annuntiationem Sermo I, printed p. 13, col. D, to p. 14, col. A (PDF pp. 37-38)

source_text: Haec postulans ac deprecans David, ad virgam, quae ex ipso pulcherrimi illius fructus florem germinatura erat, vaticinans dicebat: Audi filia, et vide, et inclina aurem tuam; et obliviscere populum tuum, et domum patris tui: et concupiscet rex decorem tuum: quoniam ipse est Dominus Deus tuus, et adorabis eum. Audi filia, quae antea in te praedicta sunt: ut et cognitionis oculis res ipsas contempleris. Audi me, tibi praesignificantem; et Archangelum perfecta tibi mysteria diserte adnuntiantem.
pass_a_gloss: These things requesting (postulans) and entreating (deprecans) David, to the rod (virga), which from him (ex ipso) the flower (flos) of that most beautiful fruit (fructus) was going to sprout (germinatura erat), prophesying (vaticinans) said: Hear (audi) daughter (filia), and see, and incline (inclina) your ear; and forget (obliviscere) your people and the house of your father: and the king will desire (concupiscet rex) your beauty (decor): since He is the Lord your God, and you will worship (adorabis) Him. Hear daughter, the things which before (antea) were foretold (praedicta sunt) in you/of you: that also with the eyes of knowledge (cognitionis oculi) you may contemplate (contempleris) the things themselves (res ipsae). Hear me, signifying beforehand (praesignificantem) to you; and the Archangel announcing (adnuntiantem) clearly (diserte) to you the perfected/fulfilled mysteries (perfecta mysteria).

choices.issue: egredietur virga de radice Iesse et flos de radice eius ascendet
choices.choice: The rod that puts forth a flower is Isaiah 11:1 (Vulgate 'egredietur virga de radice Iesse et flos de radice eius ascendet'); cited here and in section 15.
'perfecta mysteria' rendered 'the mysteries fulfilled' (perfectus as accomplished).

pass_b_english: Asking and pleading for this, David spoke in prophecy to the rod that was to put forth from him the flower of that most beautiful fruit (Isaiah 11:1), and said: Hear, O daughter, and see, and incline your ear; and forget your people and your father's house; and the King will desire your beauty, for He is the Lord your God, and you will worship Him (Psalm 45:10-11). Hear, O daughter, the things foretold of you before, so that you may also behold the realities themselves with the eyes of knowledge. Hear me, who signify them to you beforehand, and hear the Archangel, who plainly announces to you the mysteries fulfilled.
notes: Margin 'Psal. 44' is Vulgate numbering: Vulgate Psalm 44:11-12 = Psalm 45:10-11 in English Bibles; English numbering cited. The rod that puts forth a flower is Isaiah 11:1 (Vulgate 'egredietur virga de radice Iesse et flos de radice eius ascendet'); cited here and in section 15. 'rex' capitalised as King because the verse goes on 'He is the Lord your God'. 'in te praedicta' rendered 'foretold of you'. 'perfecta mysteria' rendered 'the mysteries fulfilled' (perfectus as accomplished). The faint margin note at 'adorabis eum' ('al. dele...'?) was not used.
source_notes: PDF p. 37 = printed p. 13, col. D, to PDF p. 38 = printed p. 14, col. A. Margin 'Psal. 44' (Vulgate = Psalm 45:10-11). Margin at 'adorabis eum' reads roughly 'al. dele...' (small, uncertain). 'contempleris' split 'contem-pleris' across the page turn. 'adnuntiantem' printed 'adnunciantem'.
